graph.title: GraphCtx MVP Planning Context Graph
graph.summary: This context graph captures the core ideas, product thesis, MVP direction, decisions, assumptions, risks, phase 1 build plan, success criteria, and next actions for the GraphCtx MVP project focused on converting messy AI conversations into structured context graphs and reusable Context Packs.

nodes.title: Graph-based LLM Interaction Model
nodes.body: Model LLM interaction as a graph of thinking where each node represents a question, claim, idea, research result, decision, task, assumption, source, or plan, making the graph a durable thinking workspace.

source_span.quote: Instead of treating LLM interaction as one long linear chat, model it as a graph of thinking.

nodes.title: Structured, Inspectable, Reusable Context
nodes.body: Complex AI-assisted reasoning, research, and planning require structured, inspectable, and reusable context rather than linear chat.

source_span.quote: Linear chat is not enough for complex AI-assisted thinking.

nodes.title: Focus on Context Pack Quality Before Graph UI
nodes.body: Prioritize the quality of Context Pack export before developing the graph user interface to ensure practical value.

source_span.quote: Start with Context Pack quality before graph UI.

nodes.title: Use Small Fixed Node and Edge Taxonomies
nodes.body: Adopt a small node taxonomy (idea, question, assumption, decision, risk, task, source, summary) and a small edge taxonomy (part_of, expands, supports, contradicts, depends_on, leads_to, answers) for clarity and usability.

source_span.quote: Use a small node taxonomy... Use a small edge taxonomy...

nodes.title: Phase 1 Excludes Auth, Collaboration, Cloud, and Advanced Features
nodes.body: Do not build authentication, collaboration, cloud hosting, browser extension, graph database, vector database, or advanced agent workflows in Phase 1 to focus on core MVP.

source_span.quote: Do not build auth, collaboration, cloud hosting, browser extension, graph database, vector database, or advanced agent workflows in Phase 1.

nodes.title: Users Have Long AI Conversations to Reuse
nodes.body: Target users engage in long AI conversations that they want to reuse and structure for future sessions.

source_span.quote: Users have long AI conversations they want to reuse.

nodes.title: Context Pack Export is Valuable
nodes.body: Exporting Context Packs is valuable enough for users to paste into future AI sessions, providing practical reuse.

source_span.quote: Context Pack export is valuable enough to paste into future AI sessions.

nodes.title: Graph Structure Improves Understanding
nodes.body: Using a graph structure improves understanding of complex conversations and may justify building a UI later.

source_span.quote: Graph structure improves understanding and may justify a UI later.

nodes.title: LLM May Produce Shallow Nodes
nodes.body: The LLM might generate nodes that look impressive but lack depth or meaningful content.

source_span.quote: The LLM may produce impressive-looking but shallow nodes.

nodes.title: Graph May Become Too Dense or Generic
nodes.body: If the prompt encourages one node per paragraph, the graph may become overly dense or generic, reducing usefulness.

source_span.quote: The graph may become too dense or generic if the prompt encourages one node per paragraph.

nodes.title: Visual Graph May Distract from Validation
nodes.body: The visual representation of the graph might distract users from validating whether the extracted reusable context is actually valuable.

source_span.quote: The visual graph may distract from validating whether reusable context is actually valuable.

nodes.title: Source Spans May Be Unreliable
nodes.body: Source spans relying solely on quotes may be unreliable, potentially affecting trust and traceability.

source_span.quote: Source spans may be unreliable if they rely only on quotes.

nodes.title: Build Local TypeScript CLI for Phase 1
nodes.body: Develop a local TypeScript CLI that reads Markdown or text files, extracts context graphs with an LLM, validates graph JSON, exports deterministic Markdown Context Packs, and creates a manual evaluation template.

source_span.quote: Build a local TypeScript CLI that reads a Markdown or text file, extracts a context graph with an LLM, validates the graph JSON, exports a deterministic Markdown Context Pack, and creates a manual evaluation template.

nodes.title: Produce graph.json, context-pack.md, and evaluation.md
nodes.body: The CLI command should output graph.json, context-pack.md, and evaluation.md files as deliverables.

source_span.quote: The command should produce: graph.json, context-pack.md, evaluation.md

nodes.title: Success Criteria for Phase 1
nodes.body: Five sample inputs produce valid graph JSON and readable Context Packs; at least three outputs score 4/5 or higher on Context Pack usefulness; generated Context Packs are useful for future AI sessions.

source_span.quote: Five sample inputs produce valid graph JSON... At least three outputs score 4/5 or higher on Context Pack usefulness.

nodes.title: Bootstrap pnpm TypeScript Workspace
nodes.body: Initialize the pnpm TypeScript workspace as the first development step.

source_span.quote: Bootstrap the pnpm TypeScript workspace.

nodes.title: Implement Graph Schema and Validator
nodes.body: Develop the graph schema and JSON validator before other components.

source_span.quote: Implement the graph schema and validator first.

nodes.title: Implement Deterministic Context Pack Export
nodes.body: Create the deterministic Context Pack export functionality before integrating the LLM.

source_span.quote: Implement deterministic Context Pack export before LLM integration.

nodes.title: Add OpenAI and OpenRouter Clients
nodes.body: Integrate OpenAI and OpenRouter clients behind a unified interface for LLM access.

source_span.quote: Add OpenAI and OpenRouter clients behind the same interface.

nodes.title: Run Extraction on GraphCtx MVP Planning Example
nodes.body: Test the extraction process using the GraphCtx MVP planning conversation as input.

source_span.quote: Run extraction against at least the GraphCtx MVP planning example.

nodes.title: Manually Score Extraction Results
nodes.body: Manually evaluate extraction outputs and update Phase 1 results accordingly.

source_span.quote: Score results manually and update Phase 1 results.

edges.rationale: The graph-based interaction model supports the need for structured, inspectable, reusable context.
Focusing on Context Pack quality leads to producing context-pack.md as a deliverable.
Using small taxonomies informs the design and implementation of the CLI extraction tool.
Limiting scope in Phase 1 defines the features to be built in the CLI.
Users having long conversations implies the value of Context Pack export.
The value of Context Pack export defines success criteria around Context Pack usefulness.
Building the CLI leads to producing the required output files.
Bootstrapping the workspace is the first step before implementing schema and validator.
Implementing the schema and validator precedes Context Pack export implementation.
Context Pack export implementation is followed by adding LLM clients.
Adding LLM clients enables running extraction on the MVP planning example.
Running extraction leads to manual scoring and updating results.

requiredSections.section: ## Suggested Prompt for Next AI Session

captures_main_goal.notes: The graph and Context Pack clearly capture the main goal of turning messy AI conversations into structured context graphs and reusable Context Packs.
captures_main_goal.evidence: Node n1 and n2 describe the core idea and product thesis; the summary and goal sections in the Context Pack explicitly state the main goal.

captures_key_ideas.notes: Key ideas such as the graph-based interaction model and the need for structured, inspectable, reusable context are well represented.
captures_key_ideas.evidence: Nodes n1 and n2 capture these ideas with source quotes; the Context Pack's Key Ideas section includes these with sources.

captures_decisions.notes: All major decisions from the original input are captured with rationale and source quotes.
captures_decisions.evidence: Nodes n3, n4, n5 represent decisions with source spans; Context Pack Decisions Made section lists them with rationale and related nodes.

captures_assumptions.notes: All key assumptions are included with confidence levels and source quotes.
captures_assumptions.evidence: Nodes n6, n7, n8 cover assumptions; Context Pack Assumptions section includes them with confidence and validation notes.

captures_risks.notes: All risks mentioned in the original input are present with clear descriptions and source quotes.
captures_risks.evidence: Nodes n9 to n12 cover risks; Context Pack Risks section lists them with sources.

captures_tasks.notes: Tasks and next actions are comprehensively captured with source quotes and checklist format in the Context Pack.
captures_tasks.evidence: Nodes n13 to n21 represent tasks; Context Pack Tasks / Next Actions section lists all with sources and checkboxes.

context_pack_usefulness.notes: The Context Pack is detailed and structured, suitable for reuse, but lacks explicit open questions despite the original input having an 'Open Questions' section.
context_pack_usefulness.evidence: Context Pack has an Open Questions section but states no explicit questions were extracted, which is a minor gap.

graph_coherence.notes: The graph is well-structured with meaningful edges that reflect dependencies and rationale, supporting coherent navigation of the context.
graph_coherence.evidence: Edges clearly link decisions to tasks, assumptions to value, and tasks in logical order; rationale is provided for edges.

source_traceability.notes: Every node includes a source quote from the original input, ensuring full traceability.
source_traceability.evidence: All 21 nodes have source_span with quotes; Context Pack includes source references for all items.

overall_reuse_value.notes: The graph and Context Pack provide strong reusable context for future AI sessions, with minor gaps such as missing question nodes and explicit open questions.
overall_reuse_value.evidence: Missing question nodes noted in warnings; Open Questions section empty; otherwise, detailed and structured content supports reuse.

judge.biggest_missing_value: Missing explicit question nodes and open questions reduce the ability to track unresolved issues and guide future inquiry.
recommended_changes: Include explicit question nodes extracted from the original input or flagged as open questions.
Populate the Open Questions section with any unresolved or outstanding questions to guide next AI sessions.
Consider adding source nodes or more detailed source notes to improve traceability beyond quotes.
Add more nuanced edge types or rationales to capture deeper relationships if present.
